task.title: How to Communicate and Implement Foxen Waiver to Tenants

user_message.content:
The company that I just started working for is currently using this company to offer a WAIVER to their tenants if they do not have their own renter's insurance.  There seems to be a lot of errors in the way that the property managers are communication this information to the tenants.  Evaluate the website and devise a system for me to implement this to all of the tenants of these buildings.   This information, or clause is included into their lease.  I want clear instructions how to communicate this "supplement" to the tenant that we offer (waiver) for $12.  Give me a good flow and breakdown on how to get the tenants to navigate to the portal etc. 
https://www.foxen.com/

status_update.description: Manus is working on your request

assistant_message.content: Got it! I'll evaluate the Foxen website thoroughly and then devise a clear, professional communication system and tenant flow for rolling out the renter's insurance waiver program. Let me get started.

I've thoroughly reviewed the Foxen website — the waiver program, resident portal, FAQ content, and property manager dashboard. Now I'm compiling all the key findings and best practices to build the communication system and tenant flow guide.

user_message.content: Please put this into a pdf version that I can share with my COO

assistant_message.content: I am now drafting the comprehensive communication system and tenant flow guide based on my research of the Foxen platform. Once the document is complete, I will convert it into a professional PDF format for you to share with your COO.
The guide is written. Now building the polished PDF version with professional formatting for your COO...

The PDF looks great but I can see the flow steps section is not rendering correctly due to CSS flexbox limitations in the PDF engine. Let me fix the layout to use a table-based approach for the flow steps so they render perfectly in the PDF.

Your PDF is ready to share with your COO. Here's a summary of everything the document covers across its **13 pages**:

---

**What's Inside the Guide**

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| **Section 1** | Executive Summary & Problem Statement — why communication is failing |
| **Section 2** | 5 Identified Communication Errors — with exact corrections for each |
| **Section 3** | Manager Reference — what the waiver covers vs. does NOT cover, coverage comparison table, and required legal disclaimer |
| **Section 4** | 4-Stage Standardized Communication Flow — Day 0 verbal disclosure → Day 0–1 welcome email → Day 15 follow-up → ongoing Foxen portal monitoring, plus a full decision tree |
| **Section 5** | Two verbatim email templates (Template A: Welcome & Insurance Notice; Template B: 15-Day Reminder) — ready to copy/paste |
| **Section 6** | 6-Step Tenant Portal Navigation Guide — how tenants log in, upload their COI, and check status at resident.foxen.com |
| **Section 7** | Printable Tenant Quick Reference Card — hand to every tenant at lease signing |
| **Section 8** | Insurance Policy Approval Requirements — the 5 checklist items tenants must meet to opt out, with the most common rejection mistakes |
| **Key Contacts** | All Foxen URLs, phone, email, and the critical PO Box address in one dark reference block |

---

**The single most important fix** captured in this guide: property managers must always provide tenants with the Foxen PO Box (`PO Box 12367, Columbus, OH 43212`) as the "Additional Interest" address — this is the #1 reason third-party policies get rejected and tenants continue being charged the $12 fee unnecessarily.
